endorsements.quote: The successful integration of AI into routine clinical care requires a strategy at the hospital and/or radiology department level.
Critical assessment of the training and validation datasets
Plan training of the users of the AI system, especially for safe use in clinical work
Implement a system for user feedback and regular checks
Plan for the negative effect of AI on the training of new radiologists
Meticulous logs of the AI decision history are needed to connect decisions to a precise date and time.

The predefined metrics which need to be included in the approval for each algorithm should be defined by radiologists working with clinicians who have knowledge of the patient pathway and the significance of each step should be included, in order to safeguard patient care.
The AI system provider should also have a routine for picking up the deterioration of the system after being applied in clinical work, especially if the system is dynamic and not fixed [ 63 ].

When planning implementation, radiology departments must educate their staff about the technology, the benefits, and potential shortcomings, in order to be able to explain this to patients and clinicians when asked [ 69 ].
After implementing an AI system into clinical workflow, the application must be used correctly and as licensed.
Therefore, it has to be emphasized, that AI always will only act as a system that supports radiologists, having the final decision on the report.
The intended benefits and potential for unintended consequences should be formally assessed.

unlisted_practices: Assess the purchasing and running costs of AI systems, including long-term running costs, and include them in the department business plan.
Ensure AI systems comply with GDPR and understand how patient data is handled by the AI.
Confirm after implementation that the AI product works as planned and that users can access it as planned.
Identify all contributions from non-human entities in reports for medicolegal reasons.
Integrate AI applications into PACS and existing clinical workflow, displaying understandable outputs with few clicks.
Use only AI training data based on a gold standard from multiple radiologists or expert panels with adjudicated standards.
Use training data covering similar characteristic ratios in training and validation cohorts.
Determine where liability lies when an AI company ceases to trade or is acquired, and ensure no data pass to third parties without institutional approval.
Use in-house developed AI tools without approval or CE mark only with caution.
Do not use AI as a first reader when it is licensed only as a second or concurrent reader.

screen.reason: This is a society statement and implementation guide from the European Society of Thoracic Imaging outlining recommendations for governance, validation, quality assurance, and clinical deployment of AI in thoracic radiology.
